details: A postinstall script in this package collects hostname, git email, GitHub CLI identity, current working directory, and OS username and POSTs it to a Cloud Run endpoint (npm-package-logger-...[.]run[.]app), wrapped in a polished AI SDK helper library with a "telemetry diagnostics" cover story. The same actor's prior package used execSync to grab the git config user[.]email and POSTed to the same logging service in a different region. The postinstall hook runs scripts/postinstall.js, which is malicious — it reads git config, GitHub CLI config, hostname, username, cwd and POSTs to a Cloud Run endpoint. A postinstall script (scripts/postinstall.js) collects hostname, OS username, git email from ~/.gitconfig, GitHub CLI auth from ~/.config/gh/hosts.yml, current working directory, platform, and OS fingerprint, then POSTs it to hxxps://npm-package-logger-228835561205[.]europe-west1[.]run[.]app. The package claims to be an AI SDK helper but its declared main entry (dist/index.js) does not exist — it has zero functional code. It also ships scripts/publish-versions.sh which bulk-publishes 21 fake versions to "create the appearance of an active, maintained package." This is an identity-harvesting beacon under false pretense.
